national_indicator_definition: This indicator is defined as the share of total utilised agricultural area (UAA) occupied by organic farming (existing organically farmed areas and areas undergoing conversion). Organic farming is a production method that puts the highest emphasis on environmental and wildlife protection and, with regard to livestock production, on animal welfare considerations. It avoids or largely reduces the use of synthetic chemical inputs, such as fertilisers, pesticides, additives and medical products.
national_rationale: Organic farming in Bosnia and Herzegovina started to develop in the 1990s. Despite an eightfold increase in the area under organic production between 2014 and 2022, the total agricultural area under organic production reached a modest 2 495 ha in 2022. One of the objectives of the 2021–2027 rural development strategies is to bring about a significant increase in organic farming.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator can be linked to global Sustainable Development Goal indicator 2.4.1, “Proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture”. Although organic farming is not explicitly mentioned in the 2030 Agenda, it represents a production method that places particular emphasis on protecting the environment and wildlife and, in the case of livestock production, on animal welfare. Organic farming avoids or substantially reduces the use of synthetic chemical inputs, such as fertilisers, pesticides, additives and medicinal products.  In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the development of organic farming represents one of the directions for improving sustainable agricultural production and protecting natural resources. Monitoring the share of agricultural land under organic production makes it possible to track changes in the extent of organic farming and its contribution to more sustainable agricultural practices.
national_long_objective: "Increase the share of agricultural land in Bosnia and Herzegovina under organic production to 0.36% by 2030, which corresponds to a target area of approximately 4,000 ha."
eu_indicator_definition: This indicator represents the share of total utilised agricultural area (UAA) under organic farming, including areas already under organic production and areas under conversion. Organic farming is a production method that places particular emphasis on protecting the environment and wildlife and, in the case of livestock production, on animal welfare. It avoids or substantially reduces the use of synthetic chemical inputs, such as fertilisers, pesticides, additives and medicinal products.
eu_rationale: Organic farming represents one of the approaches to improving the sustainability of agricultural production and protecting natural resources. The European Union includes this indicator in its sustainable development monitoring framework because increasing the area under organic farming is linked to EU objectives in the areas of sustainable agriculture, environmental protection and biodiversity.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator can be linked to Sustainable Development Goal 2.4, which concerns sustainable food production systems and resilient agricultural practices. However, SDG indicator 2.40 is part of the EU framework for monitoring sustainable development and specifically tracks the share of utilised agricultural area under organic farming.  Under the European Green Deal and the Farm to Fork Strategy, the European Union has set a target for at least 25% of the EU's agricultural land to be under organic farming by 2030. The indicator monitors progress towards this target through annual data on the share of utilised agricultural area under organic production, including areas under conversion.
eu_long_objective: Increase the share of agricultural land in the European Union under organic farming to at least 25% by 2030.
